spatial_claims.claim: C is a point on segment AB dividing it into AC and CB, with AC > CB
D is a different point on segment AB dividing it into AD and DB, with AD > DB
AB = AC + CB = AD + DB, so II.4 applies to both decompositions giving sq(AB) = sq(AC) + sq(CB) + 2*rect(AC,CB) and similarly for AD, DB
E is the midpoint of AB (bisection), so AE = EB; II.5 applied with AB bisected at E and cut at C (and similarly at D)
C is not at E (since AC > CB, C is between E and B); similarly D is between E and B
EC = ED together with both C and D on the same side of E implies C = D

configuration_map: All points lie on line segment AB. A and B are the endpoints. E is the midpoint (AE = EB). C divides AB with AC > CB, placing C between E and B. D divides AB with AD > DB, placing D between E and B. Both C and D are on the B-side of the midpoint E. The proof is primarily algebraic, manipulating rational and medial areas arising from these segment divisions. The one-dimensional configuration (points on a line) involves no angles, triangles, circles, or complex spatial relationships.
